text:
maya: quick sync — we need to lock down the metrics and dashboard panels for the new failure-mode taxonomy (timeouts, 5xx, OOM, degraded-mode/fallback counts, quota exhaust). need runtime + infra inputs and console UX decisions. 15m sync now? cc @kai @tomas @ariane @samira @luis

kai: can we capture per-route fallback_count and fallback_rate? need to tie each to a rollout_id/tag so we can compare canary vs baseline :eyes:

tomas: runtime can emit fallback_count and fallback_reason as labels, but we should avoid freeform strings. propose reason enum: "cache_miss", "kv_timeout", "oom_offload", "model_fallback". stack traces = no (too high-card).

ariane: from SRE POV we want counters + latency histograms for timeouts. bucket timeouts as short(0-500ms), mid(500-2000ms), long(>2s). alert if long timeouts > 0.5% per minute for top traffic routes.

samira: console: want a rollout-impact view — side-by-side baseline vs canary with delta for fallback_rate, p95 latency, and 429/5xx. expose top 5 routes by degraded impact. UX: show sparkline + relative delta.

luis: analytics: schema suggestion -> event_type, route_hash, model_version, rollout_id, tenant_hash, fallback_reason, tokens_delta, latency_ms, status_code, timestamp. We'll keep tenant and route hashed to avoid PII/high-card.

kai: a question on quotas: 429s show up in 4xx/5xx panels. do we treat quota hits as part of error taxonomy or separate quota_exhausted metric? mixing will cause noisy alerts.

ariane: separate metric please. proxy should emit quota_exhausted{route,quota_type} boolean/counter. 429 remains but quota_exhausted gives clearer signal for rollback.

Tomas: implementation notes (from runtime): we'll add these counters/exporters:
```
fallback_count{route_hash, rollout_id, reason}
degraded_enter_count{route_hash, rollout_id}
degraded_exit_count{route_hash, rollout_id}
quota_exhausted_count{route_hash,quota_type}
timeout_histogram_ms{route_hash}
```
Also emit a sampled fallback_sample event (payload redacted) to S3 for manual triage (rate-limited).

maya: cost/scale constraint: luis — we must cap cardinality. rollout_id should only be included for active rollouts (whitelist). fallback_reason must be enum. route must be hashed and optionally aggregated to service.

luis: ok on rollout whitelist and hashed route. for fallback_sample raw payloads we'll sample at 1% and store for 7 days. ETL will enrich with model_version and anonymized tenant.

samira: console API needs: GET /metrics/v1/rollout/{id}/impact?from=&to=&routes[]=... returns aggregated JSON with baseline vs canary deltas and top routes. can we get a simple contract?

kai: alerts proposal:
- fallback-rate-regression: if fallback_rate(canary) > max(1%, 2x baseline) sustained 5m for any of top-10 routes
- degraded-mode-spike: degraded_enter_count > 50/min across cluster or >20/min on a single high traffic route
alerts should reference rollout_id when available.

ariane: add runbook: auto-rollback suggestion if fallback-rate for canary > baseline by 2x AND absolute fallback_rate > 1% for 10m. include steps to disable rollout and notify owner.

maya: acting owner list and next steps:
- tomas: add counters + fallback_sample PR to runtime repo (owner)
- luis: finalize ETL schema + sampling plan
- samira: wire console panels and API contract
- kai: write alert rules and integrate into pager config
- ariane: draft runbook and test playbook
I'll own the doc and the 1-week rollout target.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: CI pipeline started for runtime/counters branch #542

tomas: pushed PR: https://git.company/repo/542 :rocket:

kai: :thumbsup:

maya: thanks all — will follow up with the doc + meeting notes and a checklist.
